where: Section 3, capacitor-rating bullet; Exam traps, 'Under-rating capacitors'; Quiz Q7 and its answer
problem: The chapter says C1 sits at 2Vp and must be rated above 2Vp, but its own Section 1 says C1 charges only to Vp. In the doubler the capacitor that stands at the full 2Vp is C2 (the output capacitor). The 2Vp figure belongs to D1's reverse voltage, not to C1. A student who follows this will fit a needlessly large C1 and may under-rate C2.
fix: C1 has only Vp across it: rate it above Vp, and note that D1 must withstand 2Vp in reverse. The doubler's output capacitor C2 must be rated above 2Vp. In an n-stage ladder the last capacitor's top plate stands at n·Vp above ground, so its rating and insulation must exceed n·Vp. Quiz Q7 answer becomes: C2, the output capacitor of the doubler (the output capacitor of the ladder in general); C1 holds only Vp.

problem: The ripple is written as ΔV ≈ I/(f·C) and then said to 'grow with n', but that formula contains no n, so nothing grows. For a cascade the ripple is larger than the single-capacitor value.
fix: Write: for the n-stage half-wave cascade the ripple grows roughly as n(n+1)·I/(2fC) and the single-stage value is ΔV ≈ I/(fC). Then the sentence about growth with n is consistent.

problem: 'Under load current I the output falls by about n·Vd plus the resistive drop' counts the diode drops twice: the formula Vout ≈ n·Vp − n·Vd already removes n·Vd at no load.
fix: Say: n·Vd is lost even at no load; on load the output falls further by the resistive and charge-transfer drop, roughly I·R_eff.

problem: 'One stage doubles, two stages triple, three stages quadruple' conflicts with the formula, where n is 'the number of stages' yet n = 2 for a doubler, n = 3 for a tripler. A student can plug n = 2 into a tripler.
fix: Use one counting rule throughout: each added diode–capacitor pair adds one Vp, so a doubler uses two of each (2Vp), a tripler three (3Vp), a quadrupler four (4Vp), and the multiplication factor equals the number of diode–capacitor pairs n.
